author: reek
body: A gauge fills the fraction of itself that its value is of its maximum, so a value above that maximum is a fraction above one, and a fraction above one is a rectangle wider than the widget it belongs to. The framebuffer compositor has clamped since it was written. This backend did not, so the same widget tree painted differently depending on which renderer walked it, and on this one the difference lands on whatever sits to the right.

author: reek
body: Nothing already in the tree could see it. The triangle count cannot: an over-wide rect is submitted and counted exactly as a correct one is, and gpu-depth-tree already reads pixels but asks only whether the fill is present at all, which it is in both cases. What distinguishes them is WHERE the fill stops, so the instrument has to scan outside the widget.

author: reek
body: The tree is a gauge pinned to a fixed width with an empty label taking the rest of the row. A label emits text and no box, so nothing but the root panel paints in the band to the gauge's right, and the root panel paints its background and its border -- neither of which is pal-primary in theme-terminal. A pal-primary pixel out there can only be gauge fill that escaped.

author: reek
body: Both readings are printed because either alone is uninformative. The outside count answers the question; the inside count is the control that says the gauge painted at all, without which a renderer that drew nothing would report a clean outside and pass.

author: reek
body: The value is half again its maximum, so an unclamped fill runs half the gauge's own width past its right edge.
